channel.title: NewsCenter — All newsletter news — 2026-11-21
channel.description: Every news received through Laurent's newsletters over the last 24 hours. 33 news received.

item.title: OpenAI turns written briefs into playable 3D experiences with Astra
item.description: GPT-6.2 Astra can turn a written brief into an interactive browser experience, such as a playable pinball game or an explorable Colosseum. OpenAI says the model ranks first on a human-evaluated 3D benchmark.

item.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Sales with ready-to-use sales workflows
item.description: ChatGPT for Sales offers workflows for selecting accounts, preparing for calls, and writing follow-ups. The plugin also includes more than 30 partner integrations, including Canva and Gamma.

item.title: Oxford researcher offers a guide to preparing children for the AI era
item.description: Daniel Susskind, an associate researcher at the Oxford Institute for Ethics in AI and a father of three, examines in his new book how to prepare children for a world in which artificial intelligence is constantly changing.

item.title: iPhone Air 2 and iPhone 18 reveal their designs through dummy units
item.description: Leaked dummy units indicate that the iPhone Air 2 will feature two rear cameras, while the standard iPhone 18 will reportedly have no notable changes.

item.title: iPhone 20 Pro could adopt a curved display with slimmer bezels
item.description: A new video allegedly shows the iPhone 20 Pro’s curved display, with significantly reduced bezels.

item.title: iPhone 20’s curved edges would be nearly invisible from the front
item.description: The future iPhone 20 design would use curved glass edges that would be virtually invisible from the front.

item.title: Apple may be reconsidering bringing an OLED display to the iMac
item.description: Apple is reportedly revisiting its plans for an OLED iMac, partly because of the cost and the lack of a sales increase seen with the OLED iPad Pro.

item.title: iPhone camera chief Jon McCormack retires
item.description: Jon McCormack, Apple’s head of iPhone cameras, has reportedly retired.

item.title: France sues Apple over planned obsolescence
item.description: Apple is being sued in France for planned obsolescence over the pairing process applied to certain iPhone and iPad components, which can cause problems when they are reused.

item.title: A major malware attack targeted iPhone and iPad users
item.description: Malicious code injected into more than 170 sites through an Optimizely vulnerability attempted to steal bank card and cryptocurrency data. iPhone and iPad users were exposed to Coruna and DarkSword exploit kits.

item.title: 24-inch M6 iMac review: a limited but convincing update
item.description: The new 24-inch iMac mainly adds the M6 chip, bringing a major boost for artificial intelligence while retaining its design and 4.5K display. It sells for 1,499 dollars and receives a score of 4 out of 5.

item.title: How to play Grand Theft Auto VI on iPhone, iPad and Vision Pro
item.description: Cloud or console streaming makes it possible to play new games such as Grand Theft Auto VI on iPhone, iPad or Apple Vision Pro.

item.title: A Caltech math course fascinates readers
item.description: In an introductory mathematics course at Caltech, a professor explained that he no longer grades homework for correctness because students use AI to complete it. Dozens of readers reacted in the comments.

item.title: Gemini can now handle multi-step everyday tasks
item.description: Google has expanded Gemini’s Tasks mode to handle tasks such as making appointments, reviewing bills, or placing grocery orders. The service asks for confirmation before certain critical steps, but Google recommends checking the results.

item.title: Google Maps generates complete itineraries for road trips
item.description: The new Ask Maps features create detailed plans, with day-by-day schedules and numbered stops, for outings or multi-day road trips. The itineraries show traffic, opening hours, and the atmosphere of places, among other details.

item.title: Claude Meetings joins Google Meet to create documents live
item.description: Anthropic has launched Claude Meetings in beta, allowing users to add Claude to a Google Meet call to create documents and whiteboards live. Users must connect Google Calendar, select the meeting, and add Claude.

item.title: The 50 Claude terms advanced users know
item.description: A glossary of 50 terms explains Claude’s essential features and concepts, including artifacts, context windows, projects, skills, and MCP. The article recommends immediately putting the terms one knows less well into practice.

item.title: Anthropic explains how Claude artifacts work
item.description: The guide presents the documents, designs, and small tools Claude creates in a panel beside the chat, along with options for editing and sharing them.

item.title: Claude details the size of its context window
item.description: This article presents the limits of paid plans and explains how Claude summarizes older messages when a long conversation approaches the context limit.

item.title: Anthropic explains search in Claude conversations and Claude’s memory
item.description: The guide shows how Claude remembers the user across conversations and how to view, edit, or pause the stored information.

item.title: The Model Context Protocol connects AI applications to data and tools
item.description: The Model Context Protocol is presented as an open standard for connecting AI applications to personal data and tools, like a USB-C port for AI.

item.title: Anthropic shows how to enable and create your own skills
item.description: The guide explains how to enable skills in the personalization settings and upload your own skills to automate tasks in Claude.

item.title: A woman buys a house with her older sister and her sister’s husband
item.description: A woman says she bought a house with her older sister and brother-in-law, an arrangement that turned out to be perfect for her.

item.title: Americans are expected to eat 46 million turkeys at Thanksgiving
item.description: The average price of a turkey has reached 28.55 dollars, up 5.5% from a year ago. Despite this, 84% of people who celebrate Thanksgiving plan to serve one.

item.title: Zone 2 cardio isn’t enough to improve fitness
item.description: Zone 2 is often presented as ideal for burning fat, improving endurance, and supporting metabolism. But athletes, doctors, and researchers say that a routine consisting only of Zone 2 is a mistake and that variety is essential.

item.title: Despite their bad reputation, cruises have never been more popular
item.description: Cruises have faced numerous warnings related to illness and incidents, but the industry continues to grow. Social media, innovation, and affordable prices have supported their popularity, even after the pandemic brought the industry to a halt.

item.title: A 19-hour business-class flight makes economy class feel regrettable
item.description: During a 19-hour flight between New Jersey and Singapore, journalist Talia Lakritz enjoyed Singapore Airlines’ meals and fully reclining bed so much that she was disappointed to arrive.

item.title: In El Paso, land bought in 1971 has remained almost unchanged
item.description: In 1971, a Business Insider journalist’s grandparents bought a residential plot of land in El Paso for 1,400 dollars, sold as a promise of prosperity. More than fifty years later, the parcel looks almost as it did then, with more litter.

item.title: The UK can no longer conceal its request for Apple data
item.description: The UK was forced to make public its requests for a backdoor into iCloud encryption. The relevant court ruled in Apple’s favor on holding the case in public.

item.title: US senators increase pressure on Apple over nudify apps
item.description: US senators questioned Apple about apps capable of generating non-consensual nude images, following concerns about teenagers’ access to them.

item.title: Cyberattack on Chase supplier exposes customer data
item.description: JPMorgan Chase confirmed a cyberattack targeting suppliers. Stolen marketing data reportedly contained more than 16,000 customer email addresses, sometimes along with phone numbers and ZIP codes.

item.title: VLC lets users keep watching DVDs on macOS
item.description: Apple began removing the technology used for built-in DVD playback with macOS 27. VLC offers a way to continue using physical media on Mac.

item.title: Run a task across multiple applications
item.description: This chapter explains how to plan a workflow, add controls, keep it short and assess its cost on Zapier, Make or n8n. It requires a connected tool, an existing automation and a repetitive task involving multiple steps.
